Pre-Incorporation & Know-Your-Customer

UBO transparency, Apostille authentication chain, official name clearance restricted wordlist, and pre-incorporation statutory fee budget.

UBO Ultimate Beneficial Owner Screening Rules Official Registry Only

>=25% ownership / control

Applicable AML statute: Ley 10/2010, de 28 de abril, de prevención del blanqueo de capitales y de la financiación del terrorismo (arts. 2-4, 14, 38, 54-56, as amended by Ley 6/2023, de 17 de marzo, de los Mercados de Valores y de los Servicios de Inversión); Real Decreto 304/2014, de 5 de mayo (Reglamento de desarrollo, arts. 12-16); Registro de Titularidades Reales (RTR) electronic filing obligations introduced by Ley 6/2023; Real Decreto Legislativo 1/2010, de 2 de julio (Ley de Sociedades de Capital, arts. 9, 408); Ley 39/2015, de 1 de octubre (administrative procedure for appeals); Arancel Notarial (Real Decreto 1426/1989); Arancel del Registro Mercantil (Real Decreto 1427/1989).
Registered Agent & Physical Address Licensed Agent Required

Conditional and restricted. The registered office (domicilio social) under art. 9 Ley de Sociedades de Capital must be a physical Spanish address where statutory mail, tax notices and legal process may be served and where management is administratively situated; pure virtual-office or post-office-box addresses are not acceptable for SL incorporation or for obtaining the AEAT NIF and TGSS employer registration code. Serviced or co-working offices with a documented right-of-use are tolerated, but the EOR must demonstrate actual operational substance at the declared address, including management presence, payroll records, personnel files and accounting archives; failure to do so creates risk of administrative domicile re-siting orders (art. 283 Ley de Sociedades de Capital) and AML commercial-substance questions.

✓ Partner licensed company-secretary channels provide local registered address and government mail forwarding.

Stage 02

Statutory Formation & Board Resolutions

Competent registry, governing statute, capital lockup rules, and first board resolution template.

Competent corporate registry

Provincial Registro Mercantil with territorial competence over the registered office; denominational name certificate obtained from the Registro Mercantil Central, Madrid.

Governing statute

Real Decreto Legislativo 1/2010, de 2 de julio (Ley de Sociedades de Capital, 'LSC'): arts. 4 (minimum share capital), 9-10 (registered office), 20-22 (deed of incorporation), 33 (registration in the Mercantile Registry) and 62 (bank-deposit certificate for cash contributions); Royal Decree 1796/2010, de 30 de diciembre, for private employment agencies (ISIC 7810).

Formation / constitutional filings

Escritura Pública de Constitución (public deed of incorporation) executed before a Spanish notary and subsequently registered (inscripción) in the Provincial Mercantile Registry, together with the Certificado de Denominación Social and the bank payment certificate.

Incorporation processing time

⚡ 22 business days (SOP sum)

Paid-up Capital & Blocked Account Regime No Capital Lockup Account Required

The SL requires a minimum share capital of EUR 3,000, fully subscribed and fully paid at the execution of the deed; cash contributions must be deposited in a Spanish credit institution and evidenced by the statutory deposit certificate annexed to the deed; instalment payments are not available for the SL and no escrow account is required by Spanish law; a single-shareholder SL (SLU) is permitted and must be declared in the deed.

Funding & unlock path:

Paid-in capital rule: The SL requires a minimum share capital of EUR 3,000, fully subscribed and fully paid at the execution of the deed; cash contributions must be deposited in a Spanish credit institution and evidenced by the statutory deposit certificate annexed to the deed; instalment payments are not available for the SL and no escrow account is required by Spanish law; a single-shareholder SL (SLU) is permitted and must be declared in the deed.

Stage 03

Tax Identity & Indirect Tax

Tax authority e-portal, entity tax classification elections, VAT thresholds, and 0% export documentation chain.

Tax ID Application Infrastructure

Competent tax authority

Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT); the official online portal is the Sede Electrónica de la AEAT (sede.agenciatributaria.gob.es).

E-government filing portal

A Spanish Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada (SL) obtains a Spanish tax identification number (NIF), ordinarily through the incorporation process and the notary's provisional-NIF application, followed by confirmation of the definitive NIF with the AEAT. The SL must file Modelo 036 to register in the AEAT census of entrepreneurs, professionals and withholding agents before commencing taxable activity. A foreign entity without a Spanish establishment that must register for Spanish VAT generally applies for a Spanish NIF using Modelo 036 and supplies evidence of its legal existence, foreign tax registration, representation and Spanish taxable activity; documents may require apostille or legalization and a sworn Spanish translation. A non-EU-established taxable person may be required to appoint a Spanish tax representative, subject to applicable exceptions and international agreements. Registration in the Register of Intra-Community Operators through Modelo 036 is required where the business needs to use a Spanish VAT number for qualifying intra-Community transactions.

Tax ID type & application path: Entity_Level_Taxation — A Spanish Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada (SL) obtains a Spanish tax identification number (NIF), ordinarily through the incorporation process and the notary's provisional-NIF application, followed by confirmation of the definitive NIF with the AEAT. The SL must file Modelo 036 to register in the AEAT census of entrepreneurs, professionals and withholding agents before commencing taxable activity. A foreign entity without a Spanish establishment that must register for Spanish VAT generally applies for a Spanish NIF using Modelo 036 and supplies evidence of its legal existence, foreign tax registration, representation and Spanish taxable activity; documents may require apostille or legalization and a sworn Spanish translation. A non-EU-established taxable person may be required to appoint a Spanish tax representative, subject to applicable exceptions and international agreements. Registration in the Register of Intra-Community Operators through Modelo 036 is required where the business needs to use a Spanish VAT number for qualifying intra-Community transactions.

Default Tax Classification & Elections

Default tax classification

Entity_Level_Taxation

Available election forms

An SL is generally a separate Spanish corporate income tax taxpayer; no US-style check-the-box election is available to classify it as a partnership or disregarded entity. Spanish tax law provides specific elections for regimes such as tax consolidation and certain special regimes, subject to eligibility and formal requirements. Spanish anti-hybrid-mismatch rules implement applicable EU and OECD measures; they do not provide a general entity-classification election.

VAT / GST & 0% Export Zero-Rating

Standard VAT / GST rate

21%

Mandatory registration threshold (Nexus)

No general domestic turnover threshold exempts a business carrying out taxable Spanish VAT activities from registration. A taxable person must register when required by the nature and commencement of its Spanish taxable activity; non-established businesses generally have no small-business registration threshold for taxable supplies in Spain.

Export 0% zero-rating conditions

Qualifying exports of goods dispatched or transported from the Spanish VAT territory to a destination outside the European Union are generally exempt with a right to deduct input VAT, provided the statutory conditions are met and the supplier retains objective evidence of export and, where relevant, the exporter's or purchaser's status. Intra-Community supplies may qualify for exemption with a right to deduct only if the substantive conditions are met, including transport to another Member State, the customer's valid VAT identification number and required reporting. Cross-border services are not automatically zero-rated: the place-of-supply rules determine whether Spanish VAT applies, and any exemption or non-taxation treatment must be supported by the applicable facts and evidence.

  • Customs export declaration and customs confirmation of exit (including the applicable electronic export-system message)
  • Commercial invoice and records identifying the goods, parties, destination and transaction
  • Bill of lading, airway bill, CMR or other transport and delivery evidence
  • Evidence supporting the customer's identity and, for an intra-Community supply, valid VAT identification and required recapitulative-statement reporting
  • Payment and accounting records; an inward remittance certificate is not a general Spanish VAT zero-rating requirement

Spain does not generally require prior real-time tax-authority clearance of every VAT invoice. Businesses within the Immediate Supply of Information (SII) regime must electronically report specified invoice-record data to the AEAT, generally within four calendar days, subject to statutory timing rules and exceptions. SII generally applies to large businesses exceeding the statutory turnover threshold, VAT groups and taxpayers registered for monthly VAT refunds. The VERI*FACTU and other invoicing-system requirements are subject to statutory scope and implementation schedules; they require compliant invoicing systems and, where applicable, transmission or preservation of records, not universal invoice pre-clearance. B2B electronic invoicing is provided for by the Crea y Crece Law, with implementation dependent on the applicable implementing rules and phased commencement. Confirm current scope and effective dates with the AEAT before deployment.

Spain imposes no general foreign-exchange repatriation deadline for export proceeds. The taxpayer must substantiate the conditions for the exemption and maintain VAT and customs records. If the conditions are not met, the AEAT may assess VAT, late-payment interest and applicable tax penalties, and may deny or recover related input-VAT deductions or refunds. Under the General Tax Law, penalties for tax underpayment can generally range from 50% to 150% of the unpaid amount depending on the classification and circumstances; separate penalties may apply for recordkeeping, invoicing or reporting failures. Fraudulent documentation may also trigger criminal liability where statutory thresholds and intent requirements are met.

Stage 04

Banking & Treasury Architecture

Central-bank FX diagnosis, tier-1 local banks vs offshore digital EMI matrix, and KYC rejection defense guide.

Foreign Exchange Regime & Central Bank Policy

Current-account convertibility

Spain is a full participant in the euro area and does not maintain exchange controls. Both current-account and capital-account transactions are freely convertible within the EU single market, subject only to statistical reporting to Banco de España and, in limited cases, national-security / foreign-direct-investment screening. Dividend and interest remittances to non-residents are unrestricted, however the payor Spanish entity must apply withholding tax on Spanish-source payments and the recipient may need tax-residence certification for treaty relief.

Export proceeds surrender rules

There is no statutory requirement to surrender euro or foreign-currency export proceeds to Banco de España or any other Spanish public body, and there is no mandatory conversion percentage. Exporters may retain proceeds in EUR or in foreign currency in authorized accounts. Only ordinary customs declarations and balance-of-payments statistical reporting obligations apply under EU and Spanish regulations.

Central bank supervision: Banco de España (BdE), acting as the Spanish national competent authority for banking supervision, foreign-exchange statistical reporting and AML/CTF coordination, in cooperation with the European Central Bank (ECB), the European Systemic Risk Board and the Spanish Securities Market Commission (CNMV).

Offshore Digital Bank / EMI Whitelist

Cross-border EMI / Fintech rails Fit: High

Feasibility for EEA-licensed EMIs is Medium: an EEA electronic-money institution (for example a Spanish-licensed EDE or passporting non-resident EMI) can open payment accounts, issue IBANs and clear SEPA transactions. Offshore non-EEA EMIs have Low viability because they cannot directly access Spanish clearing systems nor open Spanish operational accounts without a Spanish-regulated agent or partner institution. For core treasury operations and capital injections, a tier-1 domestic bank remains the primary structural relationship; an EMI may be used as an auxiliary payroll disbursement rail for low-value cross-border workers.

Core KYC Rejection Triggers & Defense Dossier

Opaque ownership or foreign parents domiciled in offshore low-tax jurisdictions without substantive economic activity.

Root cause: Opaque ownership or foreign parents domiciled in offshore low-tax jurisdictions without substantive economic activity.

Defense evidence: Apostilled corporate registry certificates for the full ownership chain, the Spanish Registro Mercantil certificate certifying the SL's shareholders, an ownership chart, audited financial statements of the ultimate parent, board meeting minutes approving the capital injection, source-of-funds documentation and a written explanation of the cross-border EOR business model.
Cryptocurrency or digital-asset inflows linked to the equity injection or operational revenues.

Root cause: Cryptocurrency or digital-asset inflows linked to the equity injection or operational revenues.

Defense evidence: Bank records of the real-money origin, exchange and wallet statements, certified valuations, a clear narrative linking digital-asset disposals to liquidity, asset-declaration documents and tax returns, plus a legal opinion confirming the legality of the digital-asset conversion under Spanish and EU law.
Discrepancy between declared EOR staffing activity and actual transaction flows, such as unexplained high-volume payments to unrelated contractors.

Root cause: Discrepancy between declared EOR staffing activity and actual transaction flows, such as unexplained high-volume payments to unrelated contractors.

Defense evidence: Executed EOR agreements, payroll calculation records, client invoices, contractor employment assignments, social-security registrations, temporary-work-license evidence (if required), and a detailed funds-flow map showing collection, retention of margin, payroll deduction and final disbursement to contractors.
Ultimate Beneficial Owner is a Politically Exposed Person (PEP) or connected to a sanctioned / restricted jurisdiction.

Root cause: Ultimate Beneficial Owner is a Politically Exposed Person (PEP) or connected to a sanctioned / restricted jurisdiction.

Defense evidence: Clear PEP declaration, complete background-check reports (credit and sanctions), letters of reference from regulated financial institutions, personal wealth and source-of-funds documentation, notarial verification of identity, and an enhanced monitoring plan approved by the bank's AML compliance unit.

Cross-Border Clearing Corridors & Settlement Fit

For inward capital injections from a non-resident shareholder, the compliant routing is a direct SWIFT MT103 customer credit transfer (or SEPA CT if the shareholder is within EEA) to the Spanish entity's Banco de España-regulated account. Purpose of payment should be stated as equity contribution/investment in capital, using ISO 20022 payment purpose code 'EQUI' (equity investment) or equivalent, with a precise reference such as 'Capital Increase – ES_SL shareholder loan/resolution date'. The receiving bank is obliged to submit the statistical declaration to Banco de España; the Spanish entity and its foreign investor must also comply with Spain's Foreign Investment Reporting (Ministerial Order and balance-of-payments rules) and may file the Declaración de Inversiones Exteriores when applicable. Due diligence requires copies of the board resolution authorizing the injection, the shareholders' ledger, the notarial deed of capital increase (if any) and an updated AML file on the paying bank.Clearing rails for operational and trade settlements include: (i) domestic and EEA payroll and supplier disbursements via SEPA Credit Transfer (SCT) and SEPA Direct Debit (SDD); (ii) non-EUR supplier or partner payments via SWIFT MT103 customer credit transfers, with strict purpose codes (e.g., 'PAYROLL', 'PROF02' professional services, 'SALE' goods/services, 'DIVI' dividends); (iii) interbank liquidity movements using MT202 COV; (iv) documentary trade transactions through commercial Letters of Credit (sight and usance) issued or advised by a Spanish commercial bank; and (v) alternative multi-cubic execution through Wise's licensed EU entity for low-value international disbursements where local FX conversion is cost-effective, provided the downstream recipient is not located in FATF/OFAC-high-risk jurisdictions. All cross-border payments must pass real-time sanctions screening and be retained with underlying supporting documentation.Outright FX forwards (EUR/USD, EUR/GBP, EUR/MXN) executed with a tier-1 Spanish bank or an EEA credit institution under ISDA/CSA termsFX swaps (sale and purchase of foreign currency against euro at two different dates) for short-term liquidity management and roll-over of export/import proceedsCross-currency interest rate swaps (EUR vs USD or other fully convertible currencies) for matching long-term loan or operational liabilitiesPlain vanilla European-style FX options, purchased for hedging currency risk on known contracted cash flows and requiring appropriateness tests under MiFID IINon-deliverable forwards (NDFs) are generally unnecessary and not commonly available for EUR because the euro is fully convertible; NDFs would only be considered if counterparties require a synthetic hedge for illiquid emerging-market currencies where local deliverability is restricted

E-commerce / gateway settlement fit: Feasibility for EEA-licensed EMIs is Medium: an EEA electronic-money institution (for example a Spanish-licensed EDE or passporting non-resident EMI) can open payment accounts, issue IBANs and clear SEPA transactions. Offshore non-EEA EMIs have Low viability because they cannot directly access Spanish clearing systems nor open Spanish operational accounts without a Spanish-regulated agent or partner institution. For core treasury operations and capital injections, a tier-1 domestic bank remains the primary structural relationship; an EMI may be used as an auxiliary payroll disbursement rail for low-value cross-border workers.

Corporate income tax return (Modelo 200) Within 25 calendar days after the 6-month period following tax year-end (July 1 to July 25 for calendar-year companies) $0 USD Late-filing surcharge of 5% to 20% of tax due plus late-payment interest; further penalties of EUR 200 to EUR 20,000 for deficient or false data
Related-party transactions informative return (Modelo 232) Concurrent with Modelo 200 (July 1 to July 25); mandatory when related-party transactions exceed EUR 250,000 per counterparty $0 USD Flat penalty of EUR 1,000 under art. 234 LGT plus interest where material related-party transactions are omitted
Deposit of audited/approved annual accounts in the Mercantile Registry (depósito de cuentas anuales) Within one month after approval by the Shareholders' Meeting (by July 31 for calendar-year companies) $50 USD Temporary closure of the corporate file (cierre registral) blocking all registry filings; administrative fine of EUR 1,200 to EUR 6,000 per non-deposited year under art. 283 LSC
Beneficial-ownership (UBO) register update through the Mercantile Registry Within 30 days of any share transfer or change in beneficial control; otherwise certified with the annual accounts deposit (by July 31) $24 USD AML administrative fines under Law 10/2010; the Mercantile Registry refuses registration of the underlying transfer deed until the UBO statement is updated

Mandatory Audit Threshold Small Company Audit Exemption Regime

Turnover: Statutory audit required when the SL meets at least two of the following thresholds for two consecutive years: balance-sheet total above EUR 2,850,000; net turnover above EUR 5,700,000; average workforce above 50 employees (art. 263 LSC). Corporate Tax & Transfer Pricing

Corporate income tax (CIT), box-by-box return breakdown, dividend WHT, and director personal liability.

Statutory corporate income tax (CIT)

25%

Dividend withholding tax (WHT)

19% on dividends distributed to non-residents (reduced by applicable treaties)

Mandatory Return Breakdown

Deadline: · Frequency:

Within 25 days following the end of the tax period (e.g., 25 January for calendar year companies)

Box-by-Box Return Breakdown (non-resident focus)

BoxField Non-resident guidanceTax-evasion pitfall
Box 1 / Line 1a (Base imponible) Taxable base calculation including adjustments Non-residents must file if having Spanish source income; use Form 210 for withholding if applicable 100 euros per day of delay, with a maximum of 1,500 euros for small companies; criminal sanctions for willful evasion
Box 2 / Line 2 (Impuesto sobre sociedades) Corporate income tax due Calculate 25% on taxable base; withholdings credited 100 euros per day of delay, with a maximum of 1,500 euros for small companies; criminal sanctions for willful evasion

Transfer Pricing & Economic Substance

Master / Local File threshold: 250,000 EUR (mandatory local file for related party transactions exceeding this threshold)

Economic substance scope: Applicable to entities performing certain activities such as holding companies, IP holding, or pure equity holding; requires adequate substance in Spain for non-genuine arrangements

Fatal Compliance Red Lines & Director Liability

Tax Evasion

Statutory sanction: Criminal penalties including fines up to 100% of evaded tax, imprisonment up to 5 years, and restitution

Director personal liability: Directors may face personal criminal liability, including imprisonment and disqualification from management
Shell Company / Lack of Economic Substance

Statutory sanction: Administrative fines up to 1 million euros, potential dissolution, and loss of tax benefits

Director personal liability: Piercing the corporate veil leading to personal liability for tax debts, possible travel bans, and criminal sanctions
AML Violations

Statutory sanction: Fines up to 2 million euros or 2% of annual turnover, criminal prosecution

Director personal liability: Personal fines, disqualification, and potential imprisonment for willful non-compliance
